title: Polynomial-Time Exact Learning of Fourier-Sparse Boolean Functions from Nearly Linear Quantum Samples
description: Research manuscript with PDF, LaTeX and review records. An algorithm exactly recovers every k-Fourier-sparse Boolean function with success at least 2/3 using O(k log^2(2k)) independent supplied uniform quantum examples and fixed-polynomial total computation and live space. Fresh residual estimates construct a queryable sign-majority hypothesis; known-function Fourier search and original-target certification contract missing Fourier energy. The theorem uses no target membership query or state-preparation inverse. Constant-confidence proposals are separated from fresh archive-safety checks; a capped adaptive progress argument tolerates unsuccessful proposals. All samples, failed trials, adaptive refits and exact rational bit costs are charged. This complements Ye's smaller sample bound with a polynomial computational guarantee. No optimal logarithmic factor, practical implementation, noise robustness, exhaustive novelty, independent peer review, formal certification or BPP/BQP result is claimed. OpenAI Codex assisted derivation, source comparison, drafting and internal checking. Version-specific review records identify the actual reviews and dispositions through Grok, Claude and AGY (configured with Gemini). These are AI reviews, not independent human peer review. Version 0.4.0 combines pruned random-hash search with local character correction, giving classical bit time tilde-O(n^2 k^3+n k^5+k^7). Exactness, sample count, success and live-space guarantees are retained. Hash formation, all bucket parities, correction, unsuccessful attempts and exact fitting costs are included.
